I'm processing the game state. My primary attacker is gone, exiled by Solitude. No blockers are needed, and I have priority. I'm focusing on my available instants or abilities to leverage this open window. Time to re-evaluate the board.


**Planning My Next Move**

I'm zeroing in on my next play. The log is unavailable, but I deduce the opponent likely evoked Solitude. My main play now hinges on the Orcish Bowmasters; the flash speed and additional value it brings feels right. I'm prioritizing this play, weighing the benefits against Fatal Push, which doesn't seem crucial right now, despite potentially saving life, and preventing blocking.


**Deciding the Best Play**

I've re-evaluated the board state now that my Thought-Knot Seer is gone. It's likely the opponent evoked Solitude. Since I can't Fatal Push it and it's going to be sacrificed anyway, the best play seems to be Orcish Bowmasters. I'll get a creature and ping the opponent for one, putting them at eight life.


**Refining the Strategy**

I'm now fully committed to the Orcish Bowmasters play. The board is set: I'll have a 1/1, a 1/1 Orc Army, and a 4/4 Construct. During my end step, my opponent will draw, triggering Bowmasters and dropping them to 8 life. The Orc Army will grow. I'm satisfied with this line of play. I'll need to attack on my next turn.


**Executing the Strategy**

I've made my decision. I will cast Orcish Bowmasters now, which will provide immediate board presence and set up the ping. The Bauble will trigger at the end step, and their draw will trigger Bowmasters, bringing them to eight life. This sets the stage for future turns, providing both board advantage and life total pressure.


**Making the Play**

I'm set to cast Orcish Bowmasters now. This play capitalizes on the end-step draw from Mishra's Bauble, guaranteeing a ping to the opponent. With my opponent's life total at 9, and the consistent board presence, I can make a play that provides both a creature, and a token, and puts them at a more precarious position.

annotations.description: Nethergoyf enters as a 0/1 with an empty graveyard, providing no immediate board presence. Against a mill opponent, Nihil Spellbomb would provide more strategic value as a proactive graveyard hate piece that could also cantrip later. Shadowspear is also arguable as it provides utility once a real creature arrives.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nethergoyf as a 0/1 on turn 1 with an empty graveyard
annotations.betterLine: Deploy Nihil Spellbomb to have graveyard interaction available, or Shadowspear to have equipment ready for a future creature. Nethergoyf could be cast later when it would enter as a larger threat.

annotations.description: Casting Shadowspear on turn 2 instead of Nihil Spellbomb against a mill deck. The opponent is playing UB Mill (Flooded Strand, Island, Archive Trap/Glimpse the Unthinkable are typical). Nihil Spellbomb would provide graveyard exile capability which could be crucial against mill strategies and also protects against the opponent potentially using graveyard-based cards. Shadowspear's +1/+1, trample, and lifelink are nice on Nethergoyf, but the equip cost of 2 means it won't be equipped until turn 3 at earliest anyway. Meanwhile, Nihil Spellbomb could sit ready to exile the opponent's graveyard (less relevant) or more importantly be available as an artifact in the graveyard to boost Nethergoyf's power via card types. However, Shadowspear is also an artifact that could end up there. The real consideration is that against a mill deck, having Nihil Spellbomb ready to crack could be important, though it exiles the opponent's graveyard, not yours. Given Nethergoyf cares about YOUR graveyard card types, and the mill opponent will be filling YOUR graveyard, Nihil Spellbomb targeting yourself would be counterproductive. So actually Shadowspear is reasonable - it provides a clock with lifelink to race the mill plan. This is debatable but not clearly wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shadowspear on turn 2
annotations.betterLine: Could have cast Nihil Spellbomb to have ready as a hedge, but Shadowspear to equip Nethergoyf and race with lifelink is a defensible aggressive line against mill.

annotations.description: The opponent has Thought-Knot Seer in hand, which is a 4/4 that will exile a card from GPT4om's hand when it enters. Nethergoyf is currently only a 2/3 (artifact and creature in graveyard after Nihil Spellbomb, but only 1 card type - artifact - so it's 1/2, or with Divest adding sorcery to GY it grows). Meanwhile, Thought-Knot Seer is a much more impactful card - it's a 4/4 body AND it exiles a nonland card from GPT4om's hand, which is devastating given the mill player's hand full of key spells like Fractured Sanity, Glimpse the Unthinkable, and Archive Traps. Nethergoyf can also escape from the graveyard later. Discarding TKS would protect the hand and remove a bigger threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to discard Nethergoyf instead of Thought-Knot Seer
annotations.betterLine: Discard Thought-Knot Seer to protect the hand full of mill spells from TKS's enter-the-battlefield exile ability and remove the larger 4/4 body threat

annotations.description: Attacked with Hedron Crab (0/2) into a board with Nethergoyf (2/3). The Crab deals 0 damage so there's zero offensive value, but the opponent can freely block with Nethergoyf to kill the Crab, which is the mill deck's key engine piece for landfall triggers.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Hedron Crab into Nethergoyf
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack. Keep Hedron Crab back safely to continue generating mill triggers off future land drops (especially with Flooded Strand and Polluted Delta in hand).

annotations.description: Declined to activate Urza's Saga to create a Construct token before declaring attackers. With only 3 mana available (Swamp, Urborg, Urza's Saga), they can't cast Thought-Knot Seer (4 mana) this turn anyway. Creating a Construct (which would be roughly 2/2 with Shadowspear + itself as artifacts) before combat would give an additional attacker alongside Nethergoyf.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities during combat, missing the opportunity to create a Construct token before attacks.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Urza's Saga's Chapter II ability to create a Construct token before declaring attackers, giving an additional 2/2 body to attack with.

annotations.description: The player discarded Polluted Delta instead of a less valuable card. With Hedron Crab on the battlefield, fetch lands are extremely powerful - each one triggers Hedron Crab to mill 3 cards. The player already has 3 Archive Traps in hand, and the opponent is about to search their library (Urza's Saga chapter III), which means all 3 Archive Traps can be cast for free. But future fetch lands provide additional mill triggers with Hedron Crab AND can trigger Archive Traps if drawn later. Meanwhile, Fractured Sanity costs UUU which is very difficult to cast with only 1 Island in play and no other blue sources, making it a reasonable discard candidate. Alternatively, one of the three Archive Traps could be discarded since having 3 is redundant when the opponent may not search again after this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Polluted Delta, losing a fetch land that synergizes with Hedron Crab for 3 cards of mill.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Fractured Sanity (very hard to cast at UUU with current mana base) or the third Archive Trap (redundant with two others already in hand and the opponent about to trigger them). Keep Polluted Delta for Hedron Crab mill triggers and mana fixing.

annotations.description: Discarding Flooded Strand to hand size is a mistake because Flooded Strand is a fetchland that serves a critical role in this mill deck. When played and cracked, it triggers Hedron Crab's landfall (milling 3 cards), enables searching the library (which lets opponents' Archive Traps be cast for free — but more importantly here, GPT4om is the one WITH Archive Traps), and provides color fixing. Meanwhile, the player has 3 Archive Traps in hand but only 1 Island on the battlefield and no way to cast Glimpse the Unthinkable or Fractured Sanity without more lands. Flooded Strand would help fix mana and trigger Hedron Crab. A better discard would be the third Archive Trap, since having 3 copies is redundant — they only work when the opponent searches their library, and the opponent (playing Eldrazi/artifacts) may not search often. Alternatively, one of the Fractured Sanity copies could be discarded since casting UUU is very difficult with current mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Flooded Strand to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard a third copy of Archive Trap or one Fractured Sanity, keeping Flooded Strand for mana fixing, Hedron Crab triggers, and future land drops

Ifnir Deadlands would have been a strictly better land drop, providing colorless or black mana (with Urborg already in play making it a Swamp too) plus a useful activated ability against opposing creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Played a second copy of Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth, triggering the legend rule and losing one to the graveyard.
annotations.betterLine: Play Ifnir Deadlands instead, which provides mana and a useful removal ability while keeping the existing Urborg in play.

The legendary rule forces sacrificing one Urborg for no benefit, losing a permanent that could have been preserved. annotations.actionTaken: Played a second Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth, triggering the legendary rule and losing a land to the graveyard for no benefit.

annotations.description: Used Drown in the Loch proactively at sorcery speed to destroy Nethergoyf (a 4/5) rather than advancing the mill game plan with Glimpse the Unthinkable. Drown in the Loch is one of their few interactive/reactive spells that can counter spells at instant speed, and spending it proactively wastes that flexibility. Additionally, the opponent can escape Nethergoyf from graveyard later. Meanwhile, Glimpse mills 10 cards which advances the primary win condition and also powers up future Drown in the Lochs and enables Visions of Beyond's draw-3 mode sooner.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Drown in the Loch to destroy Nethergoyf
annotations.betterLine: Cast Glimpse the Unthinkable to mill opponent for 10, advancing the mill win condition while saving Drown in the Loch for reactive use (countering important spells or removing threats at instant speed when needed)

annotations.description: Should play Ifnir Deadlands before casting Pithing Needle. Playing land first costs nothing and provides an additional mana source. annotations.actionTaken: Cast Pithing Needle before making land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Ifnir Deadlands first, then cast Pithing Needle

annotations.description: Gem25P Vorthos is resolving their own Pithing Needle's enter-the-battlefield trigger and must name a card. They named Urza's Saga, which is their OWN card currently on their battlefield. Pithing Needle shuts down activated abilities of the named card, so by naming Urza's Saga they are locking out their own Saga's activated abilities (the {T}: Add {C} and the {2}, {T}: Create Construct token abilities). The opponent's board has only Island and Field of Ruin — Field of Ruin has an activated ability that could be problematic (it can destroy nonbasic lands like Urza's Saga), but it requires the opponent to pay mana they may not have. Meanwhile, the opponent has Hedron Crabs in the graveyard and a mill strategy. Naming Shadowspear would also be bad since it's their own card. Given the limited choices of Shadowspear and Urza's Saga, the player should have named Shadowspear (less impactful to lock out) since Urza's Saga is actively providing value through its chapter abilities and construct token creation. However, looking more carefully at the choices presented — they could only choose between Shadowspear and Urza's Saga — both are their own permanents being offered as naming options. This appears to be an interface limitation. Naming Urza's Saga locks out their Saga's mana and construct abilities, which is a significant self-inflicted wound. Naming Shadowspear would only lock out the equip ability and the hexproof/indestructible removal ability, which is much less costly since the Shadowspear is already equipped or can remain as a static buff.
annotations.actionTaken: Named Urza's Saga for Pithing Needle, shutting down their own Urza's Saga activated abilities (colorless mana production and Construct token creation).
annotations.betterLine: Name Shadowspear for Pithing Needle instead, as losing Shadowspear's activated abilities (equip and the hexproof/indestructible removal) is far less costly than losing Urza's Saga's mana and token generation. Ideally, they should have named an opponent's card like Field of Ruin if the interface allowed it.

annotations.description: GPT4om Analyst used Surgical Extraction (paying 2 life, going to 9) to target Divest - a 1-mana sorcery hand disruption spell that is largely irrelevant at this stage of the game. The opponent has already used their discard spells and has a developed board with Thought-Knot Seer. Meanwhile, there are far more impactful targets available: Nethergoyf (which can escape from the graveyard and is a recurring threat), Emperor of Bones (two copies in graveyard, a recursive threat engine), or Urza's Saga (two copies in graveyard, and removing future copies from the opponent's library eliminates a powerful card advantage/tutor engine). Targeting Divest accomplishes almost nothing meaningful while spending 2 life that matters at 11 life against a 19-life opponent with a Thought-Knot Seer on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Divest with Surgical Extraction, removing a low-impact discard spell.
annotations.betterLine: Target Nethergoyf (removes a recurring escape threat and thins their library), Emperor of Bones (removes two copies from graveyard plus any in hand/library), or Urza's Saga (removes a powerful card advantage engine from their deck) with Surgical Extraction.

annotations.description: Failed to play a land before combat when holding Swamp and Urza's Saga. Playing Swamp precombat would give 5 mana available for post-combat plays or responses, which is relevant with Kozilek's Command and Orcish Bowmasters in hand. There's no strategic reason to delay the land drop.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed precombat main without playing any spells or lands, proceeding directly to combat.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp from hand to have 5 mana available, then proceed to combat with Thought-Knot Seer. Could also consider deploying Orcish Bowmasters precombat for an additional attacker, though waiting is defensible.

annotations.description: Paying 2 life for Surgical Extraction at 4 life drops them to 2, making them vulnerable to Orcish Bowmasters pings and cutting off potential survival lines. While Thought-Knot Seer threatens lethal next turn regardless, going to 2 life means even a Bowmasters trigger from any incidental draw kills them, eliminating any slim chance of stabilizing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Surgical Extraction (paying 2 life via Phyrexian mana) during opponent's combat at 4 life
annotations.betterLine: Consider holding Surgical Extraction and looking for a way to survive - potentially using Field of Ruin to find a land and enable casting spells next turn, or saving the life points in case a survival line opens up. If dead regardless, Surgical Extraction is fine but the life payment is a real cost when at 4.

annotations.description: At 4 life (going to 2 from Phyrexian mana), GPT4om targeted their own Hedron Crab with Surgical Extraction instead of the opponent's Nethergoyf. Nethergoyf has escape and two copies are in the opponent's graveyard - these are recurring lethal threats. Removing Hedron Crabs from their own deck/hand provides minimal value since they already have Ruin Crab in hand, while leaving Nethergoyf available to escape back is extremely dangerous at 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Hedron Crab with Surgical Extraction, removing their own mill creatures from their deck
annotations.betterLine: Target Nethergoyf with Surgical Extraction to exile both copies from the opponent's graveyard, preventing the escape mechanic from creating recurring lethal threats while at 2 life
